title: Catalog admission PRD: version-anchoring and runtime alignment
creator: Asha Patel
description: Define clear, implementable requirements for admitting new community/open model variants into Redwood's public catalog where the variant is not strictly pinned to an internal runtime build. This PRD introduces the concept of 'version anchoring' (a light-weight, documented contract between catalog metadata and runtime expectations), specifies required metadata for intake, enumerates runtime-alignment checks, and defines rollback/degeneration criteria and timelines for unanchored variants.
background: We've seen frequent ambiguity in model submissions from community weights: differences in quantization expectations, missing runtime metadata, and diverging tokenizer or special token semantics. Existing intake docs assume pinning, which causes friction for experimental variants that we want discoverable but not guaranteed. This ticket provides product-level acceptance criteria so engineering can implement automated gating and the catalog UI can surface appropriate caution and mitigation measures.
scope:
- Define mandatory manifest fields for catalog admission for unanchored community models.
- Define runtime-alignment tests that happen at ingest (small sample inference, tokenization checksum, KV cache shape sanity, quantization flags).
- Define 'version anchoring' semantics and lifecycle: soft-anchor, anchor-with-fallback, deprecate.
- Acceptance criteria and rollout/rollback timelines.
- UX copy for Console to indicate admission status and risk level.
out_of_scope:
- Full native pinning/production-reservation workflow for paid Dedicated customers.
- Large-scale performance benchmarking (these are follow-up tickets).

decisions: Adopt 'version anchoring' name for user-facing documentation instead of 'pinning' to reduce confusion for experimental variants (approved 2025-06-12).

Soft-anchor semantics: if a variant declares an anchor (model_semver + runtime_abi), runtime will prefer anchored kernels but fallback to compatible variant with explicit warning (engineering to implement fallback scoring).
Admission will be blocked if mandatory manifest fields are missing: tokenizer_checksum, model_artifact_digest, license_spdx, declared_quantization_support.
Rollback sentinel: auto-disable variant if 3 consecutive SLO violations (latency > 99p threshold) occur within first 72 hours of public exposure.
acceptance_criteria: A1: Intake API rejects submissions that lack any of the mandatory manifest fields and returns a deterministic error code and remediation guidance.
A2: Runtime alignment check runs as part of the admission pipeline and produces a short human-readable report (tokenizer mismatch / kv-shape / sample-inference outputs) attached to the catalog entry.
A3: Console shows one of three admission states for community variants: 'Soft-Anchored', 'Unanchored — Risky', 'Rejected', with clear affordances for Request Support or Mark for Enterprise Review.
A4: Engineering exposes metrics for number of soft-anchors accepted, fallback events, and first-72h SLO violations; product can query through existing telemetry endpoints.
A5: Legal verification (license_spdx present and machine-checked) completes before public tag is applied; otherwise entry stays flagged 'License Pending'.
assumptions: We can compute tokenizer_checksum deterministically from provided tokenizer files or manifest reference.
Engineering can run a short inference (<=3 prompts) against a staged runtime using ephemeral resources within the intake pipeline.
Telemetry for SLO violations is already available and can be queried by catalog admission service for initial 72h checks.
implementation_notes: Engineering will implement intake as a lightweight serverless step that validates manifest JSON, computes tokenizer checksum, and enqueues a runtime alignment job. Runtime alignment should include: tokenization round-trip, sample inference latency, KV cache shape probe. If any check fails with deterministic reasons, the variant remains 'Unanchored — Risky' until submitter fixes manifest or request a manual review.
